(2021){{cite web |title=Google Finance Reliance Power |url=https://www.google.com/finance/quote/RPOWER:NSE |access-date=21 December 2021 |archive-date=21 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211221055545/https://www.google.com/finance/quote/RPOWER:NSE |url-status=live }} | parent = [[Reliance Group]] | website = [http://www.reliancepower.co.in/home.htm reliancepower.co.in] }} '''Reliance Power Limited''' (R-Power), formerly '''Reliance Energy Generation Limited''' (REGL) is a part of the [[Reliance Group]]. It was established to develop, construct, operate and maintain power projects in the Indian and international markets. [[Reliance Infrastructure]], an Indian private sector power utility company and the Reliance ADA Group promote Reliance Power. The present CEO of Reliance Power is K. Raja Gopal since 2 May 2018.{{cite web |title=Reliance Power appoints K Raja Gopal as CEO, S Vaishnav as CFO |url=https://energy.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/power/reliance-power-appoints-k-raja-gopal-as-ceo-s-vaishnav-as-cfo/63749474 |access-date=24 March 2020 |archive-date=24 March 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200324064727/https://energy.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/power/reliance-power-appoints-k-raja-gopal-as-ceo-s-vaishnav-as-cfo/63749474 |url-status=live }} The company was the sole distributor of electricity to consumers in the suburbs of [[Mumbai]] but in 2017 they sold Mumbai operation to [[Adani Power]]. It also runs power generation, transmission and distribution businesses in other parts of [[Maharashtra]], Goa and [[Andhra Pradesh]]. With its subsidiaries, it is developing 13 medium and large-sized power projects with a combined planned installed capacity of 33,480 MW. [[Reliance Natural Resources Limited|Reliance Natural Resources]] merged with Reliance Power in 2010, shortly after its [[initial public offering]].{{cite news| url = http://in.reuters.com/article/idINSGE6610GD20100702| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20100706194732/http://in.reuters.com/article/idINSGE6610GD20100702| url-status = dead| archive-date = 6 July 2010| title = Anil Ambani mulls merging Reliance Power, RNRL | work = [[Reuters]]| date = 2 July 2010 | access-date = 2 July 2010}} As of March 2018, Reliance Power has 50 subsidiaries. In [[Fortune India 500]] list of 2019, R-Power was ranked as the 176th largest corporation in India with 9th rank in 'Power sector' category. ==Overview== The company was incorporated on 17 January 1995 as Bawana Power Private Limited and changed its name to Reliance Delhi Power Private Limited in February 1995. Its name was changed to Reliance Energy Generation Limited in March 2004, and finally to Reliance Power Limited in July 2007. {{cite news|access-date=16 January 2008|url=http://investing.businessweek.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapId=36011856|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080124114759/http://investing.businessweek.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapId=36011856|url-status=dead|archive-date=24 January 2008|title=Reliance Power Limited: Private Company Information]}} The company website identifies project sites broadly to be located in western India (12,220 MW), [[North India|northern India]] (9,080 MW) and [[North-East India|northeastern India]] (4,220 MW) and [[South India|southern India]] (4,000 MW). They include six [[fossil fuel power plant|coal-fired]] projects (14,620 MW) to be fuelled by reserves from captive mines and supplies from India and abroad, two [[fossil fuel power plant|gas-fired]] projects (10,280 MW) to be fuelled primarily by reserves from the [[Krishna Godavari basin]] (the "KG Basin") off the east coast of India, and four [[hydroelectricity|hydroelectric]] projects (3,300 MW), three of them in [[Arunachal Pradesh]] and one in [[Uttarakhand]]. ==Power generation projects== [[File:Choudwar Cuttack.jpg|thumb|Electricity transmission grid in eastern India.]] ===Coal based thermal power projects=== * [[Sasan Ultra Mega Power Project]], at Sasan village in [[Singrauli district]], [[Madhya Pradesh]] – 3,960 MW (6×660 MW). Running with full capacity from March 2015.{{cite news|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/reliance-power-commissions-third-unit-of-sasan-umpp-114032400259_1.html|title=Reliance Power commissions third unit of Sasan UMPP|date=24 March 2014|work=Business Standard|agency=Press Trust of India|archive-date=14 April 2014|access-date=13 April 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140414171952/http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/reliance-power-commissions-third-unit-of-sasan-umpp-114032400259_1.html|url-status=live}} This is designated as an Ultra mega power projects (UMPP) by the government of India. * [[Rosa Thermal Power Plant|Rosa Thermal Power Project]]: 1,200 MW (4×300 MW) coal-based thermal power plant in Rosa village, [[Shahjahanpur district]], [[Uttar Pradesh]]. The plant is fully functional.{{Citation needed|date=July 2022}} * [[Butibori Power Project|Butibori Thermal Power Project]]: 600 MW (2×300 MW), at [[Butibori]] near [[Nagpur]], [[Maharashtra]]. The plant is fully functional.{{cite news|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/Reliance-Power-starts-up-2nd-unit-of-Butibori-plant/articleshow/17866086.cms|title=Reliance-Power starts up 2nd unit of Butibori plant – Times of India|website=[[The Times of India]]|date=3 January 2013|archive-date=1 July 2016|access-date=26 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160701201119/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/Reliance-Power-starts-up-2nd-unit-of-Butibori-plant/articleshow/17866086.cms|url-status=live}} ===Gas based thermal power projects=== * Samalkot Power Project: 2,400 MW (3 x 800 MW) gas-fired thermal power project at [[Samalkot]] in [[East Godavari]] district of [[Andhra Pradesh]]. This partially implemented project is at a standstill for reasons of financial stress and lack of gas supply. Construction is not complete and whatever capacity has been installed is not being used. In 2018, Reliance power signed an agreement with the government of [[Bangladesh]] to "relocate" (or divert?) one unit from Samalkot to that country.[https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/reliance-power-signs-pacts-for-bangladesh-project/article9978945.ece Reliance Power signs agreement with Bangladesh] ===Shelved thermal power projects=== * Tilaiya Ultra Mega Power Project – 4,000 MW at Tilaiya in [[Jharkhand]] – Shelved. Reliance Power exited this project in 2015, citing delays in land acquisition. Three years later, in May 2018, it sold all remaining interests in the project to Jharkhand State Power Development Corporation for a sum of {{INR}}112 crores.{{Citation needed|date=July 2022}} * Krishnapatnam Ultra Mega Power Project at [[Krishnapatnam]] in [[Nellore district]], [[Andhra Pradesh]] – 3,960 MW (6×660 MW) – shelved. Shortly after the project was cleared in 2011, Indonesia changed its coal export policy and the project became unviable. Nevertheless, Reliance took possession of the land. In 2016, Reliance began the process of abandoning the project by seeking an exit deal with the [[Andhra Pradesh]] government. There were issues of money and bank guarantees, and the matter went into litigation. In January 2019, the Delhi High Court upheld the invocation of bank guarantees (300 crores) by the government. The project stands shelved.{{Citation needed|date=July 2022}} * Chitrangi Power Project: 3,960 MW (6 x 660 MW) – This coal-based project in Chitrangi in Singhauli district of [[Madhya Pradesh]] was canceled and shelved even before the agreement was signed. In 2011, Reliance Power won the tendering process by bidding aggressively a price of only 3.70/unit of electricity. However, it made no movement for several years. Resultantly, environment clearance lapsed in 2016 and was not extended. In March 2018, the Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation, which was the customer for the project, canceled the contract and seized the bank guarantees.[https://www.financialexpress.com/industry/uppcl-cancels-rpowers-chitrangi-power-project-seizes-bank-guarantee/1085142/ UPPCL cancels RPower’s Chitrangi power project, seizes bank guarantee] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190406124024/https://www.financialexpress.com/industry/uppcl-cancels-rpowers-chitrangi-power-project-seizes-bank-guarantee/1085142/ |date=6 April 2019 }} * Dhirubhai Ambani Energy City (DAEC) Dadri Power Project in Uttar Pradesh: 7,480 MW (shelved){{Citation needed|date=July 2022}} === Renewable energy === There is only one operational Renewable Energy (RE) project. All the rest are pending at various stages; some may have been shelved formally or informally. The projects are:{{Citation needed|date=July 2022}} * [[Dhirubhai Ambani Solar Park]] – 40 MW. This is the only operational project. ==Power distribution== * BSES Delhi (BSES Rajdhani Power and BSES Yamuna Power){{Citation needed|date=July 2022}} * BSES Kerala{{Citation needed|date=July 2022}} * BSES Odisha{{Citation needed|date=July 2022}} ==Order to Shanghai Electric== [[Anil Dhirubhai Ambani]] placed a single order for $8.3 billion with [[Shanghai Electric Group Company]] (SEC) for buying 36 coal-fired thermal power generation units, spare parts, and related services over a 10-year period.{{Citation needed|date=July 2022}} ==Loans from Exim bank== Reliance Power Ltd. signed an agreement with the US Export-Import Bank in 2010 for a $5 billion loan to finance power projects. The loan will finance 900 megawatts of renewable technologies such as solar and wind energy,{{cite web|title=US Exim Bank to fund Reliance Power's solar expansion|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/US-Exim-Bank-to-fund-Reliance-Powers-solar-expansion/articleshow/12697795.cms|work=The Times of India|access-date=22 June 2012|date=17 April 2012|archive-date=18 April 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120418022308/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/US-Exim-Bank-to-fund-Reliance-Powers-solar-expansion/articleshow/12697795.cms|url-status=live}} as well as up to 8000 MW of gas-based power generation technology, the Indian company said in a statement. This $5 billion agreement is in addition to the $917 million already approved by the Ex-Im Bank for Reliance Power's coal-fired power plant at Sasan in central India. The agreement will allow Reliance Power access products and services at competitive rates and help create manufacturing and services jobs in the US.{{Cite web |title=Reliance Electric GV3000 Drive 10V4160 {{!}} Automation Industrial |url=https://10v4160.com/blog |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=10v4160.com |language=en}} The loan will also enable quicker access to the bank's long-term dollar loans. Reliance Power signed a pact with the US's General Electric Co. (GE) worth {{INR}}100 billion ($2.2 billion) to implement a 2400 MW power plant. The plant will be located in the southern Indian town of [[Samalkota|Samalkot]] and the pact was signed during the visit of President Barack Obama.{{cite web|title=Reliance Power Secures Loan, Signs Deal with GE, Others|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052748703856504575601641127438662|work=The Wall Street Journal|access-date=22 June 2012|author=JOHN SATISH KUMAR|date=8 November 2010}} ==Initial public offering and controversies== In 2007, Reliance Power issued a red herring stating an intention to go public with an IPO. The proposed IPO was to fund the development of its six power projects across the country whose completion dates are scheduled from December 2009 to March 2014.{{cite news|access-date=16 January 2008|url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/2008/01/05/stories/2008010552360100.htm|title=Reliance Power set to raise over Rs 10,000 cr via IPO|date=5 January 2008|last=Noronha|first=Paul|archive-date=2 December 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081202172053/http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/2008/01/05/stories/2008010552360100.htm|url-status=live}} The [[Securities and Exchange Board of India]], the organisation which regulates activity in the [[India]]n [[stock market]], placed some restrictions based on a complaint about the formulation of the IPO. {{cite news|access-date=15 January 2008|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/StoryPage/StoryPage.aspx?id=392927ca-da53-48c8-a772-e6c7edc0dce2&&Headline=SEBI+puts+curbs+on+Reliance+Power+offer|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080123045744/http://www.hindustantimes.com/StoryPage/StoryPage.aspx?id=392927ca-da53-48c8-a772-e6c7edc0dce2&&Headline=SEBI+puts+curbs+on+Reliance+Power+offer|url-status=dead|archive-date=23 January 2008|title=SEBI puts curbs on Reliance Power offer|date=28 December 2007|last=Layak|first=Suman}} The complaint also resulted in a [[public interest litigation]] being filed against the company. However, the [[Supreme Court of India]] passed a ruling that the IPO would go ahead even if any order is passed by any Indian court against the venture.{{cite news|access-date=15 January 2008|url=http://www.indianexpress.com/story/260624.html|title=Reliance Power can go ahead with IPO: Supreme Court|date=12 January 2008|last=ENS Economic Bureau|archive-date=16 January 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080116052624/http://www.indianexpress.com/story/260624.html|url-status=live}} The IPO opened on 15 January 2008 and attracted $27.5 billion of bids on the first day, equivalent to 10.5 times the stock on offer, thereby creating India's IPO record. The upper cut off price for the bid was [[Indian Rupee|₹]] 450 {{cite news|access-date=15 January 2008|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/apps/news?pid=20601091&sid=aKNhjpoMWGj8&refer=india|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130118171911/http://www.bloomberg.com/apps/news?pid=20601091&sid=aKNhjpoMWGj8&refer=india|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 January 2013|title=Reliance Power Record IPO Gets $27.5 Billion of Bids|date=15 January 2008|last=M.C. Govardhana Rangan|first=Archana Chaudhary}} A media report pointed out that, if the company's stock price were to cross ₹650–700, Anil Ambani would go past L. N. Mittal to become the richest Indian.{{cite news|access-date=16 January 2008|url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/News/News_By_Industry/Energy/Power/My_father_would_have_been_a_happy_man_Anil_Ambani_on_REPL_IPO/articleshow/2703375.cms|title=father would have been a happy man: Anil Ambani on REPL IPO|date=16 January 2008|last=Times News Network|archive-date=16 February 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080216231720/http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/News/News_By_Industry/Energy/Power/My_father_would_have_been_a_happy_man_Anil_Ambani_on_REPL_IPO/articleshow/2703375.cms|url-status=live}} "It is a reflection of world community in the future of India... Investors seem to be confident in the future of Indian economy," Indian Finance Minister, [[P. Chidambaram]] told the media about the IPO. {{cite news|access-date=16 January 2008|url=http://www.rediff.com/money/2008/jan/15rpl.htm|title=Reliance Power IPO subscribed 10 times in 4 hrs|date=15 January 2008|agency=Press Trust of India}} Reliance Power debuted on the stock markets on 11 February 2008. However, the markets were still reeling after the January 2008 stock market [[volatility (finance)|volatility]], and concerns over speculation that the issue was overpriced sent the stock plummeting soon after its listing. At the end of the first day, the stock traded at a value that was 17 percent lower than its issue price of ₹450.{{cite web|url=https://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-business/Hard-lessons-from-the-primary-market-fiasco-financial-scene/article15410276.ece|title=Hard lessons from the primary market fiasco financial scene|date=18 February 2008|work=The Hindu}} Investors who were betting on the stock reaching 1.5 or even twice its issue price lost a fortune in the process. On 25 February, in an effort to mitigate investor losses, Reliance Power decided to issue 3 bonus shares for every 5 shares held.{{cite web|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/report.asp?newsid=1152793|title=Reliance Power offers 3:5 bonus, share cost now Rs 269|date=25 February 2008}} ==Carbon credits== On 2 February 2011, [[United Nations]] registered Reliance Power's Sasan Power Plant to be eligible for earning [[carbon credit]]s followed by Krishnapatanm Ultra Mega Power Project and Tilaiya Ultra Mega Power Projects.{{Cite news|date=2011-02-04|title=RPower gets nod for carbon credits|language=en-IN|work=The Hindu|url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/companies/RPower-gets-nod-for-carbon-credits/article15127585.ece|access-date=2021-12-21|issn=0971-751X|archive-date=21 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211221055546/https://www.thehindu.com/business/companies/RPower-gets-nod-for-carbon-credits/article15127585.ece|url-status=live}} United Nations issues carbon credits to companies that employ advanced technologies in reducing carbon emission. These carbon credits can then be sold to those companies that are emitting more than their statutory emission. ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== * [http://www.reliancepower.co.in/ Official website] * [http://www.sourcewatch.org/index.php/Reliance_Power Reliance Power] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150108051241/http://www.sourcewatch.org/index.php/Reliance_Power |date=8 January 2015 }} at SourceWatch {{Portalbar|Companies|Energy}} {{Reliance Anil Dhirubhai Ambani Group}} [[Category:Companies based in Mumbai]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 1995]] [[Category:Reliance Group subsidiaries]] [[Category:Electric power companies of India]] [[Category:1995 establishments in Maharashtra]] [[Category:Energy companies established in 1995]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]]

Reliance Power Limited (R-Power), formerly Reliance Energy Generation Limited (REGL) is a part of the Reliance Group. It was established to develop, construct, operate and maintain power projects in the Indian and international markets. Reliance Infrastructure, an Indian private sector power utility company and the Reliance ADA Group promote Reliance Power. The present CEO of Reliance Power is K. Raja Gopal since 2 May 2018.
The company was the sole distributor of electricity to consumers in the suburbs of Mumbai but in 2017 they sold Mumbai operation to Adani Power. It also runs power generation, transmission and distribution businesses in other parts of Maharashtra, Goa and Andhra Pradesh. With its subsidiaries, it is developing 13 medium and large-sized power projects with a combined planned installed capacity of 33,480 MW.
Reliance Natural Resources merged with Reliance Power in 2010, shortly after its initial public offering. As of March 2018, Reliance Power has 50 subsidiaries. In Fortune India 500 list of 2019, R-Power was ranked as the 176th largest corporation in India with 9th rank in 'Power sector' category.
